participant_roles: State (interface): IMaintenanceState (Start, Complete, Cancel, Status); Abstract state with the default behaviour: MaintenanceStateBase (every operation throws ApiException 409 unless overridden); ConcreteState: ScheduledState (overrides Start and Cancel); ConcreteState: InProgressState (overrides Complete and Cancel); ConcreteState, terminal: CompletedState (overrides nothing); ConcreteState, terminal: CancelledState (overrides nothing); Context: MaintenanceContext (picks the state from the persisted Status by dictionary lookup; Start/Complete/Cancel delegate to the state; TransitionTo changes it); Client: MaintenanceService.TransitionAsync; Persisted state: MaintenanceSchedule.Status (enum MaintenanceStatus); Subject of the side effects: Car (Status, IsAvailable)
intent_and_evidence: Problem: a maintenance job may only move SCHEDULED -> IN_PROGRESS -> COMPLETED, or be cancelled before completion, and each move has a different effect on the car. MaintenanceContext selects the state object from Schedule.Status (FlemanApi/Service/Maintenance/MaintenanceContext.cs:28) and forwards Start/Complete/Cancel to it (lines 31-33). ScheduledState.Start refuses a car that is not AVAILABLE, otherwise takes it out of service and calls context.TransitionTo(InProgressState.Instance) (FlemanApi/Service/Maintenance/ScheduledState.cs:16-29). InProgressState releases the car on Complete and Cancel (FlemanApi/Service/Maintenance/InProgressState.cs:13-18). The two terminal states inherit the 409 default for every operation. MaintenanceService contains no switch or if on Status; the only uses of Status there are the due/overdue query predicates. Each concrete state is a stateless shared instance (Instance), so no state object is allocated per request. Executed evidence: MaintenanceStateTests (18 cases), MaintenanceServiceTests (20), MaintenanceFleetAvailabilityTests (2).
change_description: Added: IMaintenanceState, MaintenanceStateBase, four concrete states, MaintenanceContext, client MaintenanceService, entity MaintenanceSchedule. Reason: the workflow of the new maintenance feature. No baseline collaboration is replaced: the baseline had no maintenance workflow.

participant_roles: State (interface): IMaintenanceState (Start, Complete, Cancel, Status); Abstract state with the default behaviour: MaintenanceStateBase (every operation throws ApiException 409 unless overridden); ConcreteState: ScheduledState (overrides Start and Cancel); ConcreteState: InProgressState (overrides Complete and Cancel); ConcreteState, terminal: CompletedState (overrides nothing); ConcreteState, terminal: CancelledState (overrides nothing); Context: MaintenanceContext (picks the state from the persisted Status by dictionary lookup; Start/Complete/Cancel delegate to the state; TransitionTo changes it); Client: MaintenanceService.TransitionAsync; Persisted state: MaintenanceSchedule.Status (enum MaintenanceStatus); Subject of the side effects: Car (Status, IsAvailable)
intent_and_evidence: Problem: a maintenance job may only move SCHEDULED -> IN_PROGRESS -> COMPLETED, or be cancelled before completion, and each move has a different effect on the car. MaintenanceContext selects the state object from Schedule.Status (FlemanApi/Service/Maintenance/MaintenanceContext.cs:28) and forwards Start/Complete/Cancel to it (lines 31-33). ScheduledState.Start refuses a car that is not AVAILABLE, otherwise takes it out of service and calls context.TransitionTo(InProgressState.Instance) (FlemanApi/Service/Maintenance/ScheduledState.cs:16-29). InProgressState releases the car on Complete and Cancel (FlemanApi/Service/Maintenance/InProgressState.cs:13-18). The two terminal states inherit the 409 default for every operation. MaintenanceService contains no switch or if on Status; the only uses of Status there are the due/overdue query predicates. Each concrete state is a stateless shared instance (Instance), so no state object is allocated per request. Executed evidence: MaintenanceStateTests (18 cases), MaintenanceServiceTests (20), MaintenanceFleetAvailabilityTests (2).

participant_roles: Subject (interface): IBookingEventPublisher (Subscribe, Unsubscribe, PublishAsync); ConcreteSubject: BookingEventPublisher (keeps List<IBookingEventObserver>; subscribes every injected observer in DI order; PublishAsync notifies each one and isolates failures); Observer (interface): IBookingEventObserver.OnBookingEventAsync(BookingEvent); ConcreteObservers: EmailBookingObserver (customer e-mail through IEmailService), AuditLogBookingObserver (one structured log entry); Event passed to observers (push model): record BookingEvent with enum BookingEventKind; Client that raises events: BookingService.PublishBookingEventAsync, called from CreateBookingAsync, ModifyBookingAsync and CancelBookingAsync; Wiring: CH04 block in Program.cs; Role note: the subject is a separate publisher object, not the BookingHeader domain object itself
intent_and_evidence: Problem: customers must be told when a booking is created, modified or cancelled, each event must be audited, and a further reaction must not require editing BookingService. BookingService publishes one BookingEvent after each successful save and names no reaction. BookingEventPublisher loops over a copy of its observer list and calls OnBookingEventAsync on each (FlemanApi/Service/Notifications/BookingEventPublisher.cs:36); an observer that throws is logged and skipped, so the others still run and the HTTP result is unchanged. Adding a reaction means one IBookingEventObserver class and one registration line. The CREATED e-mail text is the baseline text moved unchanged into EmailBookingObserver. Executed evidence: BookingEventPublisherTests (6), BookingObserverTests (7), BookingServiceNotificationTests (5).
change_description: Added: IBookingEventPublisher, BookingEventPublisher, IBookingEventObserver, EmailBookingObserver, AuditLogBookingObserver, BookingEvent, BookingEventKind. Reason: booking lifecycle notifications and audit. It takes over the direct BookingService -> IEmailService call of the baseline, which was not a catalogued pattern instance, so no instance is replaced or removed.
